did.abstract: Organized in 1879 to "cultivate the public taste for music," the University Musical Society sponsors concert series, opera, dance and theater performances at the University of Michigan. The records consist of director's files of Albert A. Stanley, Charles A. Sink, Gail Rector, and Kenneth Fischer; correspondence relating to performances and management of the Society; ledgers and account books, board of directors minutes and packets; files concerning the Choral Union, the University of Michigan School of Music, the Henry S. Frieze Memorial Organ Fund, and Hill Auditorium; learning resources created by UMS for arts education; recordings of performances; also visual materials and audiotapes of Board meetings.
did.physloc: Portions located in offsite storage; prior notification required for access.

acqinfo.p: Material from the UMS (donor 2996) was first received in 1953. Accessions are received periodically. Additional material was received from O'Dell, Hewlett, and Lukenbach Associates (donor 11667) in 2017 and Edward Poindexter (donor 11193) in 2020, and Kenneth C. Fischer (donor 11868) in 2018.

accessrestrict.p: The records are open for research use with the exception of recent executive officers files.

p.emph: Access Restrictions for University of Michigan Records

blockquote.p: University records are public records and once fully processed are generally open to research use. Records that contain personally identifiable information will be restricted in order to protect individual privacy. Certain administrative records are restricted in accordance with university policy as outlined below. The restriction of university records is subject to compliance with applicable laws, including the Michigan Freedom of Information Act.

Categories of Restricted Records
Executive records: Records generated by the university's executive officers, deans, directors, department heads, and their designated support staff are restricted for twenty (20) years from the date of their creation.
Restricted files are indicated in the contents list of the collection’s finding aid with a restriction note indicating the restriction type and the date of expiration.

For further information on the restriction policy and placing Freedom of Information Act requests for restricted material, consult the reference archivist at the Bentley Historical Library (bentley.ref@umich.edu) or the University of Michigan Freedom of Information Office website (https://foia.vpcomm.umich.edu/).

userestrict.p: Copyright of material produced by the University Musical Society is held by the Regents of the University of Michigan but the collection may contain third-party materials for which copyright is not held. Copyright to portraits of artists may be held by the artist. Patrons are responsible for determining the appropriate use or reuse of materials.

bioghist.p: The University Musical Society was organized in 1879 by members of the university faculty called together by University President Henry S. Frieze. In 1881 it was incorporated as a nonprofit educational corporation. The society twice extended its corporate existence. In 1969 it was reincorporated "in perpetuity."

The society states that its purpose is to, in part, "cultivate the public taste for music and afford opportunities for the acquisition of musical knowledge and skill..." Affiliated with it, but technically governed by separate boards, were the Choral Union, the University Orchestra and the Ann Arbor School of Music. Despite their technical independence, in reality interlocking directorships led to a situation in which members of the UMS Board of Directors administered the various subordinate units.

In 1892 this situation was formally recognized. The independent governing boards of the Choral Union, Orchestra, and School of Music were disbanded and all three institutions came directly under the jurisdiction of the UMS directors. The school's name was changed to the University School of Music, and funds were raised for the construction of a building for the school.

The Choral Union itself was an outgrowth of the Messiah Club and consisted of singers from several Ann Arbor churches as well as the university community. This organization has continued its traditional Messiah performances as well as participation in May Festival concerts.

In 1893 it was proposed that the society's concert series close with a festival of three concerts rather than with a single event as had been the custom. The three-day event was a great success and, in 1894, the May Festival became an annual occurrence.

While always closely associated with the university, the UMS was and remains technically independent from the control of the Board of Regents. Generally satisfactory, this situation proved troublesome regarding musical education. In 1905 the Regents authorized Michigan students to perform accredited studies at the UMS-governed University School of Music. In 1929 the regents and UMS agreed that the University School of Music should become a component part of the University of Michigan, however the school would continue to be administratively under the control of the UMS Board of Directors whose decisions would be subject to the approval of the regents.

In 1940 the University Musical Society relinquished all rights and responsibilities regarding the School of Music to the regents of the University of Michigan who agreed to assume full responsibility for the school's operation. This separation was both legal and physical as the society left its offices in the School of Music to occupy offices on the first floor of Burton Memorial Tower.

The Choral Union Series, begun in 1889, has served as the major series of concerts presented by the UMS. Presentations have included major orchestras and artists from around the world. The Philadelphia Orchestra began a tenure with the May Festival in 1936, an association which lasted until 1984. Interest in presenting an expanded base of concerts led to the establishment of the Chamber Arts Series in 1963 which focused on chamber music. A Summer Concert Series took place from 1964 to 1971.

In 1960 the University Musical Society recommended changes to Hill Auditorium to allow for an orchestra pit and proscenium which would make possible the introduction of ethnic folk dance, ballet and opera presentations as well. These performances also took place in Rackham Auditorium and, beginning in 1971, the Power Center for the Performing Arts. Hill Auditorium would not undergo any significant renovations until 2002.

In addition to the above series, the University Musical Society also sponsors special (non-subscription) concerts. Among these have been special recitals by Arthur Rubenstein, Marian Anderson, and Vladimir Horowitz. The University Musical Society and School of Music have also sponsored benefit concerts for the School of Music featuring artists of international repute with the University Symphony. Many world premieres of choral and orchestral works have been commissioned by the University Musical Society and performed by the Choral Union.

The 1970s saw the creation of the UMS Advisory Committee, a group of volunteers who functioned as an adjunct to UMS in charge of organizing social functions. Throughout the years, the Advisory Committee (who were renamed UMS Ambassadors in 2014) has organized the May Festival Prelude Dinners, lead the Bravo! cookbook project and launch, ushered for UMS school day performances, and planned the Ford Honors Gala, in addition to many other dinners, receptions, and cocktail parties. These social events broadened community involvement and, although the festive events were not fundraisers, provided important financial support to UMS by engaging a new donor base.

In the 1980s and 1990s the University Musical Society faced the challenge of the increasing costs of performances and of the need to raise a considerable portion of the operating budget through gifts. The latter led to an expansion in the development efforts of the staff. There was also a perceived need to offer a more varied choice of performances in order to attract patrons of all ages and musical taste. The work space occupied by the UMS, Burton Tower, and Hill Auditorium, its major venue, were both in need of renovation. Changes and activities documented in the 1990-1998 accession include the demise of the May Festival and the beginning of the Distinguished Artist Award--the last May Festival took place in 1995; the Distinguished Artist Award was first awarded in May 1996--and the development of a renovation plan for Hill Auditorium. The plan was approved by the Regents in September 1990 and fund raising began as part of the university's Capital Campaign.

Ken Fischer was a long-standing UMS president from 1987 to 2017. During his tenure, he grew the organization and expanded programming to include new art forms outside of classical music and brought in more diverse artists. After a patrons' study report was conducted in the early 1990s, UMS increased its engagement with K-12 education, additional academic units within the university, and across the general community in Southeast Michigan. Increased engagement with younger audiences came through the Youth Education Program, which under Ken Fischer sponsored school day performances of select performances. The program also created extensive teaching resources and curriculum supplements for teachers to use in the classroom, reinforcing UMS's role in local arts education. Under his leadership, UMS explored partnerships with collaborators across the world and received numerous grants to put the organization on better financial footing.

In the 21st century, UMS continued to produce classical music concerts and events while also expanding the repertoire to include contemporary dance, world music, pop, country, rock, and avant-garde theater performances. In 2012, with support of the Creative Ventures Leadership Fund, UMS launched UMS Pure Michigan Renegade--a series of boundary-pushing performances that brought important and unique works into Ann Arbor's cultural conversation, such as the historic 2012 remounting of Robert Wilson and Philip Glass's Einstein on the Beach.

Ken Fischer retired from UMS in 2017, after 30 years as President. He was succeeded by Matthew VanBesien. In March of 2020, the COVID-19 pandemic forced UMS to cancel the final months of its 2019/20 season. The planned 2020/21 season was subsequently cancelled as well, although throughout the shutdown UMS offered virtual programming. UMS resumed operation with its 2021/22 season.

scopecontent.p: The records of the University Musical Society document its founding in 1879, governance and administrative restructuring through the years, its activities sponsoring musical, dance and theatrical performances on campus, and its role in music and arts education. The records include directors' correspondence files, board of directors minutes, ledgers and financial records, photographs, sound recordings and videotapes.

The records are organized into seventeen series: Board of Directors, Directors' Correspondence, President's Correspondence, Executive Directors' Files, Committees, Financial records, Historical file, Topical Files, Contracts, Photographs, Staff Files, Scripts, Motion Pictures (film, videotape and digital materials), Sound Recordings, Outsize Bound Volumes, Outsize Scrapbooks, Outsize Photographs.

relatedmaterial.head: Related Material
relatedmaterial.p: Performance programs, posters, flyers, brochures, printed marketing material, and additional learning resources can be found in the University Musical Society (University of Michigan) publications collection at the Bentley Historical Library.

The Ann Arbor District Library and the University Musical Society have collaborated on an online collection of UMS programs and photographs titled UMS: A History of Great Performances. The site includes digitized, full-text searchable concert programs from 1879 to 2025 and a selection of photographs of performers, UMS staff, concert patrons, and venues. The UMS website also includes a searchable database of performances and repetoire called UMS Rewind.

scopecontent.p: The Board of Directors series is divided into four subseries: Miscellaneous Files; Minutes/Financial Reports; Meeting Packets; and Audiotapes. The Miscellaneous subseries contains several folders of primarily correspondence dating from 1976 to 1983.

The minutes were bound and the pages consecutively numbered through June 1989. This series includes thirteen bound volumes (1876 through June 1989) and loose minutes (July 1989 on). Both the bound and the loose minutes include related items documenting the activities of the Board of Directors, its Executive Committee and the following UMS committees: Development, Long-Range Planning/Implementation, Budget and Finance and Marketing. Minutes of the annual meeting of the University Musical Society are included in the Board of Directors Minutes. Earlier minutes of the UMS are found in earlier accessions. Please consult the summary contents lists for information about the complete run of minutes.

The Board of Directors Packets were maintained by UMS staff. Included in the packets are agendas and minutes (which may duplicate materials in the previous series) and additional background information prepared for the board members, including reports from standing committees such as Development, Marketing, Programming, and Long-Range Planning.
The audiotapes of Board of Directors meetings (99 cassettes) span 1954-1988, but do not provide a complete run of the meetings.

scopecontent.p: The Director's Correspondence, 1898 to 1983 (boxes 1-64, 68-98, 103-106) series covers the tenures of directors Francis W. Kelsey, Charles A. Sink and Gail W. Rector. The series is organized by year and thereunder alphabetically by correspondent. There are occasional exceptions to this, for example, correspondence with or related to the National Association of Concert Managers, 1956-1962, is all filed under 1956 (box 79). This file reflects Charles Sink's important role within that organization.

Certain portions of the correspondence from the Rector years have been sampled, among these are correspondence from contributors, thank you notes from school groups and others receiving complimentary tickets, complaints, and "fan" letters. The large volume of inquiries received annually by Mr. Rector from both agents and performing artists interested in participating in a UMS concert series have not been retained.

Prior to 1941, correspondence regarding the School of Music is also found in this series. In general, however, the early correspondence is of low research value, serving the UMS as a general office file and containing great quantities of routine information about ticket purchases and other predictable concerns.

This series contains correspondence relating to events sponsored under the auspices of the University Musical Society. When attempting to locate artist correspondence in this series, it is recommended that the researcher look under both the artist and agent names. The greater bulk of correspondence with regard to individual artists is handled through the agent, rather than the artist themselves. There are, however, exceptions to this rule.

The Philadelphia Orchestra and May Festival folders contain a large amount of correspondence from conductor Eugene Ormandy, often providing insights into his ideas regarding programming and interpretation of specific works. Correspondence of other May Festival participants can also be found in various May Festival folders. A number of letters from composer Aaron Copland are included in the 1976 folders. He conducted several of his works in that year's May Festival.

Many artists of outstanding international repute are also represented in this series. Vladimir Horowitz gave several performances for the UMS and his correspondence is located in the folders of his agent, Harold Shaw, for the years 1976 and 1978. A list of Horowitz's personal requests for a performance is included, as is correspondence with his wife, Wanda Toscanini Horowitz, who discusses the presentation of a film honoring her father that was to be presented in conjunction with a performance of her husband.

In 1981 Alberto Ginastera was commissioned to write a piano concerto to be premiered by Anthony di Bonaventura at a UMS concert. Correspondence related to this event is located in the Thea Dispeker Artists folder. The 1982 Ann Arbor Summer Festival folder includes transcripts of two interviews Gail Rector conducted with French mime Marcel Marceau.

A large number of artists are represented in the 1983 and 1984 Gail Rector 25th anniversary folders. These are indicative of the relationships Rector established with these artists during his tenure with the University Musical Society.
Files dated 1976 and 1977 include letters from Dr. Jack Kevorkian, who was involved in the production of a video of UMS Messiah performances.

As stated above, this collection does not attempt to represent the hundreds of inquiries for performance received by Mr. Rector. However, evidence of the scope of these inquiries can be found in many of the agent folders.

scopecontent.p: The President's and Executive Director's Correspondence series includes one folder of correspondence created by UMS President Charles Sink regarding the May Festival, 1928 and 1930-1935. The correspondence of President Gail Rector covers the years 1984 through July 1987 when Rector retired as president of the University Musical Society. The correspondence of Executive Director Kenneth Fischer begins in 1987 and continues through 1988. The correspondence is organized alphabetically; the 1988 files include two folders of correspondence organized in chronological order.

The correspondence documents communication with artists' agents, artists, concert goers and other arts managers. Included is documentation of the Ann Arbor Summer Festival (AASF) with which Gail Rector was active. Ann Arbor Summer Festival Board of Trustees minutes, and files related to the AASF Executive Committee, Programming Committee and Marketing Committee were not kept as they can be found in the papers of Eugene Power also held by the Bentley Library. Eugene Power founded the festival in 1978.

For the first few years of Kenneth Fischer's tenure as executive director, the UMS staff used the same alphabetical filing system for correspondence. Additional later correspondence, not filed alphabetically, is also included under his sub-series. With Fischer's tenure, a topical file, not broken by year, was also instituted (see Topical Files below).

scopecontent.p: The series includes records of the executive director, Kenneth Fischer. Included are administrative records, comprising general records, strategic planning documents, development files, and budget and financial records. Also included are material about Fischer's speeches and talks, involvement in external organizations, clippings and press, and photographs.

A topical files sub-series includes material on various projects, events, and programs. The folder "Hill Auditorium Renovation, 1990-1992" contains a detailed "History of Hill Auditorium At the University of Michigan" by Ernest O. Moore written for the Office of the University Planner in 1978. Subsequent reports detail the planning and execution of the Hill Auditorium renovation in the early 2000s. The "Love Letters" folders contain congratulatory letters and letters thanking Kenneth Fischer and the UMS staff from performers, patrons, community leaders, impresario colleagues and musical professionals, members of the UM and Ann Arbor communities and friends. Thank you letters were sent for tickets received, presentations made, for community service performed, and, in general, for the quality of presentations provided by the University Musical Society. Other materials include photographs of a celebratory party held for Fischer, documents on proposed regional partnerships, business correspondence, and annotated board meeting minutes and strategic planning documents.

scopecontent.p: The Committees series consists primarily of Advisory Committee records and one folder and an outsize bound volume of financial records. The Advisory Committee folders include minutes and related correspondence. The minutes from 1975-1995 tend to be scattered and do not provide a complete run of Advisory Committee meetings, whereas the minutes from 1996-2007 are comprehensive. Also included with the Advisory Committee materials is Together: A History of the UMS Advisory Committee and Ambassadors documenting the committee's genesis, responsibilities and achievements over its 45 year existence.
There is also one folder of material on the Finance Committee

scopecontent.p: The series titled Historical File includes the original articles of association, bylaws and revisions through 1968; several histories of the UMS; records of the Choral Union and School of Music; and various reports. Also included is correspondence from former director Gail Rector featuring his recollections of artists and performances at UMS during his directorship.

scopecontent.p: A wide array of subjects is covered in the Topical Files series. Records and correspondence that document the inception of the first Ann Arbor Summer Festival are included, as are similar materials for the Fair Lane Festival, a summer endeavor of the University Musical Society that took place in 1967, on the grounds of the Henry Ford estate on the University of Michigan-Dearborn campus. Of additional interest is a folder that lists the world premieres presented by the UMS and two folders of historical materials which include a letter and prints of Jenny Lind, the legendary Swedish singer of the late nineteenth century. Additional material includes a musical autograph of violinist and composer Fritz Kreisler.

scopecontent.p: The Contracts series provides copies of the final contracts for performances for the years 1933/34-1984/85. The earlier seasons tend to be represented more completely than the later. Contracts for seasons in the 1970s and 1980s are not represented in their entirety. For the most part, these files include only contracts, no accompanying correspondence. Cover letters and related correspondence are found in the Correspondence series. Contracts from 1986-2017 are closed to researchers.

The Photographs series is organized into five subseries: Facilities, Portraits, Artist and Performances, UMS, and Captioned Photographs. The Facilities file contains pictures of Hill Auditorium. The Portraits subseries consist of pictures of members of the UMS Board of Directors and UMS officers.

Artist and Performance Photographs include several oversized mounted prints of performances from May Festivals in 1918, 1943 and 1946. The bulk of the series consists of artist photographs for concerts from the 1957/58 season through 1977/78. These photographs were maintained by the UMS along with the corresponding programs. In the 1968/69 and subsequent folders, reviews of concerts are also included. The majority of the photographs came from the artists themselves, and most of them are also autographed. The boxlist includes a note of those photographs for each year that were taken locally, many of them at Hill Auditorium. In locating a photograph of a given artist, it may serve the researcher well to first look through the programs included in the UMS Publications, and then locate the corresponding folder of photographs.

UMS photographs created by Ken Fischer in the 1990s document his duties as executive director, staff development, concerts, travel around the United States and abroad, and other special events.
Captioned Photographs consists of approximately 70 photographs ranging from 1913-2006 with captions written by UMS Director of Artistic Programming and Production Michael Kondziolka. Captions include identifying information and sometimes short anecdotes from Kondziolka. The photos depict a variety of UMS events, performances, featured artists, and staff members. Subjects include Hill Auditorium's first audience, onstage and backstage photos from events at Hill, the annual May Festival, and candids of artists on tours around U-M and Ann Arbor. Artists who appear include Isaac Stern, Mstislav Rostropovich, Nadja Solerno-Sonnenberg, and Patrick Stewart. It is unclear for what purpose these images and captions were compiled, and duplicates may exist elswehere in the collection.

scopecontent.p: The Staff Files series documents the efforts of the Youth Education staff and of the Events and Donor Relations staff. Included are educational packets featuring curriculum material created by UMS for teachers. These packets are evidence of UMS's efforts in the 1990s and early 2000s to engage more with K-12 students, including planning special performances for local children. Additional learning resources and teacher guides can be found in the UMS Publications series.
Correspondence and planning related to development events are included in this series.

scopecontent.p: The Video Recordings document various performances sponsored by the University Musical Society. Formats include VHS videotapes, and DVCAM and DAT digital video tapes, 16mm film, digital files. The VHS tapes include the Distinguished Artist Award of the Ford Honors Program (1996-1998 and 2001-2002), the Hill Auditorium Re-opening Concert in January 2004, special performances by the Grand Rapids Symphony, and the Youth Performance Series (2001-2003). The Royal Shakespeare Company (RSC) residency videotapes include lectures by Ralph Williams, professor of English Language and Literature at the University of Michigan, delivered prior to the performance of the history plays in 2001 and the Merry Wives of Windsor and Coriolanus in 2003. There are several tapes documenting the RSC performance of Salman Rushdie's work Midnight's Children. A copy of the rehearsal script will be found in the Scripts series. Digital materials document a performance by singing group Sweet Honey in the Rock at Hill Auditorium in 2004, the 2004 Merce Cunningham Residency, and Distinguished Artist awards.

Also in the series are two 16mm films, one entitled A Conductor Speaks featuring Arthur Fiedler and Gail Rector. The other, When Heaven and Earth Move, is a 15 minute film documenting the history of the annual May Festival, produced to honor its 100th anniversary. An interview with legendary UM band director William Revelli is also captured on videotape.

scopecontent.p: Sound Recordings include material on cassette, reel to reel tapes, and LP as well as digital audio recordings. LP formats include the 100th anniversary celebration, and a 1978 recording of the performance of Messiah. The digital audio recordings include Haydn's "The Creation," St. Matthew Passion," and William Bolcom's "Songs of Innocence and Experience."

Also included in this series are performance and rehearsal excerpts, conversations, and interviews surrounding the Ann Arbor May Festival, including a celebration of the 75th May Festival by UMS director Gail Rector, and a compilation of sound bites from the 1973 May Festival featuring UMS staff and supporters, as well as artists such as Eugene Ormandy, Isaac Stern, Van Cliburn, and Jessye Norman. Additionally there are recordings of selected performances, mainly taking place in Hill and Rackham Auditoriums, from the 1960s-1990s that were digitized UMS historian Richard LeSeuer.

scopecontent.p: The series Scrapbooks consist of two scrapbooks commemorating the 100th anniversary of the University Musical Society in 1979. "The University Choral Union", a yellow, 3-ring scrapbook, measures 13 x 19". It contains material dating from 1969 to 1979, including newspaper clippings, photographs, and programs concerning University Choral Union concerts and performers. "The Festival Chorus", a blue, 3-ring scrapbook, measures 13 x 20". It contains material dating from 1971 to 1979, including newspaper clippings, photographs, and programs documenting UMS concerts and performers.
